distinguishing_features: Localized laser shock peening of the wheel-seat fillet to create a deep compressive residual-stress layer.
Direct modification of the fillet's local mean stress field rather than sensor-derived monitoring, derating, or operating-envelope restriction.
Manufacturing/in-shop surface treatment applied to existing axle material and geometry without new telemetry or control logic.
Targets rail-axle wheel-seat fillet fatigue initiation rather than turbine-liner cracking, flare-tip erosion, or blade creep.
parsed.objective_technical_problem: Increase fatigue resistance of a rail axle wheel-seat fillet by reducing the local tensile stress state that drives crack initiation without changing axle geometry or operating duty.

parsed.non_obvious_reason: Inducing compressive residual stress by peening a fatigue-critical fillet is a conventional, obvious way to reduce tensile mean stress, so the LSP application is not an inventive step even though the listed prior art is remote.
